briefing.opening: Hello everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for October 12, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Warnings
sections.content: News released today once again reminds us of the severe impacts of climate change globally. Specifically, forums emphasizing the urgent need for tailored countermeasures against increasingly frequent extreme weather events such as heatwaves, droughts, and floods have been held domestically [6, 8, 10]. Internationally, concerns have been raised by experts that the Scottish rainforest restoration project is becoming more complicated due to climate change, alongside warnings from 'Bukang-i' [4] [60, 67, 70]. Furthermore, a report has been released stating that the El Niño phenomenon, intensified by global warming, could lead to nearly 500,000 excess deaths by February [62], raising awareness about the potential human cost of the climate crisis. In the Sydney region, a complete fire ban has been imposed due to high temperatures of 37 degrees Celsius and the risk of wildfires caused by 'dry lightning' [73], illustrating how the direct threats of climate change are becoming a reality in various parts of the world.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Efforts and Achievements
sections.content: Various local governments in Korea are making active efforts to achieve carbon neutrality goals. Suwon Special City is encouraging citizen participation, with Mayor Lee Jae-joon emphasizing the completion of carbon neutrality through the participation and practice of all citizens, and hosting events such as the 'Carbon Neutrality Hanmadang' [11, 16, 21, 24]. Incheon City has strengthened its commitment to the 2045 carbon neutrality goal, showing positive results with a 22% increase in greenhouse gas reduction last year compared to the previous year [12, 13, 14, 20, 27, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37], but reduction performance in the agriculture, livestock, and fisheries sectors was low, indicating the need for additional efforts [23, 29]. Gwangmyeong City is reflecting citizen opinions in its carbon neutrality policies and smartly supporting citizen-led carbon neutrality practices by transitioning its 'Climate Volunteer Carbon Piggy Bank' app service [15, 17, 18, 22, 25]. Asan City Council and Yongin Special City Council are strengthening their policy foundations by respectively activating special committees for carbon neutrality policy review and holding discussions on implementation measures through a circular economy [19, 28].

sections.title: 🌱 Climate Change Adaptation and Agricultural Innovation
sections.content: In response to climate change, innovative adaptation efforts are continuing in the agricultural sector. NH NongHyup Seed & Bio's 'Cheongmyeong Gaeul' variety has been recognized as the best variety in Korea, showcasing a successful example of agricultural technology responding to climate change [1]. Furthermore, efforts to disseminate smart farming technologies to respond to abnormal weather and climate change are gradually expanding [2], and some advanced farmers are pioneering new ways to overcome both rural aging and climate change simultaneously through the mechanization of 'millet' cultivation [7]. Education and awareness-raising efforts are also active. Gimpo City is raising awareness among future generations by operating AI and climate change experience booths at the Student Convergence Experience Festival [3], and Choi Jae-chul, Chairman of the Climate Change Foundation, emphasized wise responses in the era of climate crisis through a special lecture on 'Survival Strategies in the Era of Complex Crises and AI' [5]. These efforts are expected to contribute to enhancing the overall societal adaptability to climate change.

sections.title: 🌍 Opportunities and Challenges in Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is a major growth engine both domestically and internationally, while also presenting complex challenges. Renewable energy has emerged as the top new business entry sector for Korea's top 1,000 listed companies [38, 42, 45, 46, 47, 48, 49, 53, 57], indicating that businesses perceive renewable energy as a future growth driver. Particularly in the United States, the explosive increase in demand for Energy Storage Systems (ESS) due to the spread of renewable energy and advancements in AI is creating new opportunities for Korean companies [52], but the high cost of ESS is still cited as a major obstacle to the energy transition [44]. Meanwhile, the cost of turning LNG power plants on and off to fill power gaps caused by the intermittency of renewable energy has doubled in five years [41], and concerns about cybersecurity are growing, with 8,500 renewable energy systems in Europe reportedly vulnerable to hacking [55]. A joint investigation into the fatal fire at a Yeongdeok wind turbine that occurred last March was conducted after six months [56], highlighting the need for continuous attention and investment in the safety management and stable operation of renewable energy facilities.

sections.title: 📰 International Community's Call for Climate Action and Awareness Expansion
sections.content: The international community is recognizing the urgency of climate change and raising its voice to call for action. In Brussels, Belgium, tens of thousands of citizens participated in a protest, urging the European Union (EU) for stronger climate action [59, 65]. Furthermore, news that dismissed government scientists are seeking new ways to disseminate information about climate change [58] emphasizes the independence of climate science and the importance of communication with the public. Efforts to raise climate change awareness are also continuing in the arts and culture sectors, such as the Manneken Pis statue, a symbol of Belgium, wearing a special 'climate change' costume [69]. This demonstrates that responding to climate change should not be limited to specific sectors but requires broad societal interest and participation.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has balancedly highlighted the severity of the climate crisis, diverse response efforts both domestically and internationally, and the opportunities and challenges in the renewable energy transition process. Climate change is everyone's responsibility and an opportunity, and we must build a better future through continuous attention and cooperation. This concludes today's climate briefing.
